filter_note: V1 set (7) + market briefing + AI news; Today window ≈ Oct 6–7 PT

market_briefing.lede: Agents that act across company lines are getting rules: Sierra and Meta proposed an open protocol for personal agents dealing with businesses, and Salesforce called for zero-trust checks on every agent interaction. Assistants and GTM data vendors are also moving into the files and agent tools reps already use.

bullets.text: Agent-to-business protocol: Sierra (Oct 6) announced the Personal Agent Protocol with Meta, Genesys, Shopify, Stripe, Walmart and others: OAuth sessions, company-set permissions, and routes via website, MCP/OpenAPI or the company's own agent. A v0.1 spec is planned later in October.

Skills inside the doc: Claude for Google Workspace (public beta, Oct 6) brings Claude's connectors and saved skills into Docs, Sheets and Slides. Anthropic's example pulls Salesforce account history into a QBR deck, and edits wait for approval by default.

Data sold to agents: HG Insights (Oct 6) launched a Contextual Intelligence Platform with an MCP server, agents reachable from Slack and Teams, and consumption pricing in Intelligence Credits. Copilot modules start at $22,000.

biggest_ai_news.title: OpenAI publishes 722 math manuscripts from an unreleased model
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 6: 372 result families on GitHub from ~4,000 attempted problems, many with Lean proofs. None are peer reviewed, and the model has not been released.

biggest_ai_news.title: Anthropic puts Claude inside Google Docs, Sheets and Slides
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 6: public beta on paid plans. The same day, Claude for Startups added a free year of Claude Team and $1,000 in API credits.

biggest_ai_news.title: Microsoft and Nvidia launch Surface Laptop Ultra on RTX Spark
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 7: up to 128GB unified memory and 1 petaflop of AI compute for local workloads. Windows security features plus Nvidia OpenShell control what on-device agents can access.

biggest_ai_news.title: Google opens SynthID Detector to everyone
biggest_ai_news.body: Oct 7: available globally in English. It checks images, video and audio from Google and partners including OpenAI and NVIDIA.

what_changed.title: Sierra and Meta propose a standard for personal agents dealing with businesses
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent, not watchlist). Oct 6: Personal Agent Protocol, developed with Meta, Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart. Sessions run on OAuth, customers choose read or write access, and companies decide what agents can do via web pages, MCP/OpenAPI APIs or their own agent. The v0.1 spec and a reference implementation are due later in October. Why it matters: buyer-side agents may arrive with scoped credentials, so agent-facing surfaces become part of sales and service.

what_changed.title: Claude for Google Workspace brings connectors and skills into Docs, Sheets and Slides
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent). Oct 6: sidebar add-on in public beta on all paid plans, plus beta connectors to create and edit Google files from Claude. 'Ask before edits' is the default mode. Enterprise controls (Compliance API, CMEK, OpenTelemetry audit export) apply to the add-on.

what_changed.title: HG Insights repackages GTM data as an agent layer with credit pricing
what_changed.body: NEW (adjacent GTM data). Oct 6: Fabric data foundation (new Momentum signal), Copilots with explainable Fit/Need/Intent scoring, HG Agents and a Superagent reachable from Slack, Teams or MCP, and an MCP server also offered via AWS Marketplace. Pricing is consumption-based Intelligence Credits; Copilot modules start at $22,000.

what_changed.title: Salesforce publishes a zero-trust view of multi-agent systems
what_changed.body: Low signal, not a launch. Oct 7 newsroom post by Kathy Baxter summarizes a white paper from workshops with 21 organizations. It calls for deterministic guardrails outside the agent's reasoning loop, an 'owner's tag' on every memory item, and defined human escalation points. No new product PR from any watchlist company Oct 6–7.

what_changed.title: OpenAI backs mandatory incident disclosure (carried from Oct 6)
what_changed.body: Not new. At Australia's AI inquiry, OpenAI said its handling of an agent breach was 'not good enough' and said it would support a mandatory incident-disclosure framework.

quiet_note: Quiet Oct 6–7: no net-new product PR from Salesforce, Gong, Clay, Nooks, Outreach, Salesloft or Monaco, and no Clay pre-announcement ahead of Sculpt. Salesloft named a Chief People Officer (Oct 6), filed to its competitor page. Aged off Today: OpenAI EU text watermark, Reflection Beam, GPT-6 speedups and Cohere North 2 (all Oct 5). X pull unavailable again (API returned 402 Payment Required).

watch.title: Clay Sculpt tomorrow (Thursday, Oct 8)
watch.body: No pre-announcement found as of Wednesday morning. The 9:30 AM opening keynote (Kareem Amin with Clay's heads of product and AI) promises "a first look at what Clay is building next"; a main-stage session covers an agent that reads workflow logs and fixes routing bugs via PR. The closing fireside is with Sierra co-founder Clay Bavor, two days after Sierra's Personal Agent Protocol. Watch for pricing on skills and agents.

interpretation.fact: No watchlist product PR Oct 6–7. Sierra announced the Personal Agent Protocol with Meta and partners (Oct 6). Anthropic launched Claude for Google Workspace in beta and expanded Claude for Startups (Oct 6). HG Insights launched its Contextual Intelligence Platform (Oct 6). OpenAI released 722 math manuscripts (Oct 6). Microsoft and Nvidia launched the Surface Laptop Ultra, and Google opened SynthID Detector globally (Oct 7). Salesforce published a multi-agent trust post (Oct 7); Salesloft named a CPO (Oct 6).
interpretation.note: Light interpretation: identity, permission and audit standards for agents are forming outside the CRM vendors, so they are likely to show up as requirements for GTM agents that touch buyers or customer data. PAP is a proposal with no published spec yet.
